import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import skew

# Right-skewed dataset (common in real-world data)
np.random.seed(42)
data = {
    'salary': np.random.exponential(scale=50000, size=100),
    'house_price': np.random.lognormal(mean=11, sigma=0.5, size=100),
    'transaction_amount': np.random.exponential(scale=200, size=100)
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Check skewness of each column
print("Skewness BEFORE log transform:")
for col in df.columns:
    print(f"  {col}: {skew(df[col]):.3f}")

# Apply log1p transform (log(x+1)) to handle zeros
df_log = np.log1p(df)

# Compare skewness before and after transformation
print("\nSkewness AFTER log transform:")
for col in df_log.columns:
    print(f"  {col}: {skew(df_log[col]):.3f}")

# Print results
print("\nOriginal data (first 5 rows):")
print(df.head())
print("\nLog-transformed data (first 5 rows):")
print(df_log.head())
